query: How can we reduce declined expense submissions?

per_column.name: asset_type_category
per_column.rationale: The kind of asset is a property of the expense, not an intervenable policy lever, but it can plausibly influence both what gets submitted/how and whether it is declined; treated as a background common-cause characteristic rather than a settable treatment.

per_column.name: submission_pattern
per_column.rationale: Whether a submission is automatically_generated vs user_initiated vs travel_related reflects a submission process that an organization could actually change (e.g., alter auto-generation rules), making it an intervenable lever on declines.

per_column.name: requisition_source_department
per_column.rationale: Department is largely a fixed structural attribute driving both the type/pattern of submissions and decline rates; not a lever one would set, so it functions as a confounder to adjust for.

per_column.name: expense_description_specificity
per_column.rationale: How specific the description is (product_model_named vs generic_category_only) is something submitters can be required to change via policy/templates, and plausibly affects declines -- an intervenable treatment.

per_column.name: travel_expense_flag
per_column.rationale: Whether an expense is travel-related is an intrinsic property of the expense, not a settable lever; it can influence submission pattern and decline likelihood, so it acts as a confounder.

per_column.name: ci_identifier_quality
per_column.rationale: The quality/format of the configuration-item identifier (standard_model_number vs generic_placeholder) is a configurable data-entry property that can be enforced and plausibly affects declines -- an intervenable lever.

judge.rationale: The query 'How can we reduce declined expense submissions?' is genuinely interventional, and several added columns capture settable levers (submission pattern, description specificity, CI identifier quality) rather than immutable traits, so an intervenable treatment is present. However, the schema is weak on the confounder requirement: the columns tagged as confounders (asset type, department, travel flag) are more naturally common characteristics/attributes than well-motivated common causes explicitly adjusting treatment-outcome bias, and none are richly established as confounders. No confounder was named in the query, which is favorable for demonstrating capability, but their plausibility as true common causes (rather than mediators or mere descriptors of the same expense) is only moderate, yielding limited confounder quality.
